summary: Finished slice 2 (documentation) of revision 2. Added the programmatic streak (`sheenTrigger`) to documentation/features.md, documentation/examples.md, documentation/configuration.md, README.md and documentation/development.md, each with a working example and the rules that it works with or without `focusSheen`, on split/disabled/busy buttons, and that reduced motion disables both triggers with no override. Strengthened the reduced-motion wording in docs/features/zest-button-focus-sheen/guide.md and added three A3 documentation tests to __tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx. The code, CSS, hook, api.md and guide parts from the earlier attempt were already present and verified unchanged. Ran the build and the full suite (371 tests, all passing).

tests.name: R7: the value on mount plays nothing and the first change plays one sweep on an unfocused button
R7: changing while a sweep is playing restarts it (parity flips)
R7: setting the same value again plays nothing, but a number-to-string change counts
R7: works with focusSheen omitted, false and true
R7: several quick changes each restart and no queue builds up
R7: a trigger while focused plays the programmatic layer as well as the focus layer
R7: repeated triggers after the animation has ended still replay
R7: the first value never plays on mount
R8: a split control sweeps once across the whole control per trigger change
R8: a disabled button plays one sweep without becoming usable or firing its click handler
R8: a busy button plays a sweep and keeps its aria-busy and spinner state
R8: a disabled button never shows a focus streak
R8: a button that is both disabled and busy plays exactly one sweep per change
R8: the sweep is not restarted when the busy state ends part-way
R8: the band is visible on the disabled colours of every style
R9: reduced motion removes both bands entirely, with no override
R9: the rule is a live media query applied to regular, split and both triggers
R9: reduced motion leaves the focus ring and other feedback alone
A3: the API page lists sheenTrigger, its string|number type, absent default and first-value-on-mount rule
A3: features, examples, configuration, README and the guide show a sheenTrigger example and say it works with or without focusSheen
A3: the pages say reduced motion disables both triggers and that no prop overrides it
A1: the value on the first render is inactive and plays nothing
A1: each later value change returns an alternating active result, including number to string
A1: setting the same value again returns the same result and does not replay
A1: React Strict Mode double effects still play each change exactly once
A1: it uses no listener, timer or storage and leaves no timer behind
